industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

memo.verdict: Park on price, not on quality. Bullish on the business, neutral on the shares at EUR 267.5 (2026-10-09). secunet Security Networks is a crisp 'Demand Inflection' in a certified near-monopoly, and the shares have already paid for it: the modal total shareholder return on our path is 6.7 percent a year over eighteen months (to 2028-04-09) and 8.6 percent a year over three years (to 2029-10-09), against a 20 percent bar. Progress to Early-Stage if the price returns to the entry zone of about EUR 200 to 224 (the three-year and eighteen-month clearing prices on the modal path), or if the Q3 2026 cash and the FY2027 guidance move our path toward consensus without the price moving. Conviction: medium on the business case; medium-high that the return at this price is below the bar. The park rule is not triggered: management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C, none at D or F.
case: Legislated German and European spending on defence cryptography, sovereign cloud and border security, with mandatory EU cyber and identity rules, is lifting demand for secunet's certified SINA products at sector level with more than two years of visibility: the EUR 100bn special fund, the proposed EUR 500bn infrastructure fund, NATO's trajectory to up to 5 percent of GDP by 2035, Germany's 2027 draft raising core procurement 55 percent to EUR 30bn; the Entry/Exit System live across 29 Schengen states from April 2026, NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, eIDAS 2.0, a quantum-safe mandate from 2030. The company's order book confirms it: H1 2026 intake EUR 287.4m (+78.7 percent), book-to-bill 1.4x, backlog EUR 360.8m. German cybersecurity spending grew 10 percent to EUR 12.2bn in 2026 while GDP was flat, so the demand has decoupled from the economy.

secunet captures a disproportionate share because it holds the only BSI approvals to GEHEIM for SINA workstations, gateways and, since May 2025, cloud; multi-year audit cycles block entrants; secrets encrypted for decades lock customers to the original certified provider; public authorities accepted FY2025 list-price rises without buying less. Public-sector revenue grew 29.4 percent in H1 2026 and group intake grew about four times as fast as Bechtle's. The moat is national, not international, and the regulator that grants it could loosen it; that is where the 'Foundations' are fragile.

The internal change is continuity, not transformation: a chief executive promoted from the parent on 2025-07-01 (Marc-Julian Siewert, operator-track at Veridos, also described as a highly constrained corporate administrator); a strategy (sovereign cloud and AI platform by 2030; partnerships with HPE, NVIDIA, Cloudflare, DCSO, Tenzir) articulated and resourced; certified new products (SINA Cloud to GEHEIM, quantum-safe SINA hardware, SCOPE x SINA Cloud); international revenue +39.4 percent to EUR 25.4m; guidance specified to the upper end but EBIT reconfirmed, not raised; the SysEleven acquisition (2022, EUR 61.3m) written down by EUR 17.4m in 2025; the payout corridor cut to 30 to 50 percent in March 2026; services 10.5 percent of revenue and falling.
counter_case: The strongest case against is the false friend our risks research described before the H1 2026 report, and the H1 numbers strengthen it on cash. secunet's reported growth is an illusion of timing and working capital. H1 2026 revenue +19.2 percent is flattered by a 2025 comparison depressed by the federal budget delay until September 2025; part of the 29.4 percent public-sector growth is catch-up. The EUR 80m inventory build and the EUR -60.1m operating cash flow are the top line bought with cash: inventories EUR 144.7m, cash EUR 6.9m, short-term borrowings drawn, net debt EUR 22.8m. The gross margin at 19.9 percent, down from 30.1 percent in FY2021, shows the growth arriving as low-margin hardware on a fabless model dependent on single-source chips and Lenovo-class partners. The Business Sector (-47.4 percent, EBIT EUR -5.3m) shows what happens where certification does not protect: against agile multinational vendors and hyperscalers with vastly superior firepower, secunet loses. Services fell to 10.5 percent of revenue, so the sovereign-cloud and recurring-revenue story has not started; the one scorecard it has, SysEleven, is a EUR 17.4m write-down. The board that decides what to do with the cash and the 20 percent authorised capital is the parent's: 75.12 percent held, one independent director of six, insiders with 1,000 shares, short-term loans to the parent in treasury operations. The regulator that grants the moat is widening the roles in which commercial off-the-shelf devices and open-source multi-vendor architectures are permitted. The 65 to 70 percent of results that land in Q4 make the year a single bet on the Bundestag passing defence and digital line items between September and November 2026, with the EUR 100bn special fund facing exhaustion and one house arguing 2026 defence outlays could fall EUR 7bn below 2025. A budget slip in that quarter lands on EUR 6.9m of cash and leaves the company drawing a EUR 45m line to carry stock it cannot ship; three consecutive negative cash quarters are the sell trigger. The shares, at 30x the earnings two years out on a 24 percent float trading about 6,370 shares a day, 40 percent above the 200-day average after a 58 percent rise in three months on no company news the research can explain, in a sector the environment reads as orders up, shares down, de-rate to the sector's 20x in a week; the mark-to-market downside with earnings unchanged is 16 to 33 percent, and the 2021 to 2024 precedent of earnings per share falling from EUR 6.66 to EUR 4.32 while the multiple compressed from above 80x is the precedent for worse. Consensus, with two to three contributors, already sits above the company's own EBIT guidance and above our path, so there is no beat left to deliver and the sell-side has been chasing the price rather than leading it: the consensus target is below the price.

What the record concedes: the comparison effect, the cash strain, the hardware mix, the governance and the thin float are all true and are why 'Foundations' is C, 'Case Riskiness' is C and the 'Modal return' at this price is F; the Business Sector and the cloud transition are not in our path's margin assumption; we cannot refute the cash point from the accounts until the Q3 2026 statement. What the record holds on the business: the backlog is contractual and covers over 80 percent of the H2 revenue consensus expects; the 2018 and 2025 episodes show budget delays defer rather than destroy demand and arrive first as cash-flow shocks, which is exactly the H1 2026 pattern; FY2025 converted an H1 outflow of EUR -9.0m into EUR 62.5m for the year; the moat is renewed, not eroded, by the May 2025 GEHEIM cloud approval, the quantum-safe approvals and the 2030 mandate, and no commercial off-the-shelf substitute is approved at SECRET level; the order intake and public-sector growth are sector phenomena that a change of chief executive at a 75 percent-owned subsidiary does not produce; and it is consensus, not the company, that sits above guidance. What the record holds on the price: the counter-case and our own arithmetic agree on it.
triggers: - Price: progress to Early-Stage at about EUR 200 to 224 on the modal path (about EUR 200 at eighteen months on the adverse drop-through); B returns to the 'Investment Thesis' below about EUR 224.

- Q3 2026 interim statement (early November 2026): operating cash flow positive and above EUR 40m confirms; below EUR 20m is the alarm; a negative Q3, a third consecutive negative cash quarter, invalidates; inventories materially down by the FY2026 report.

- Bundestag budget sessions September to November 2026: defence and digital line items for 2026 and 2027 passed; not passed by November 2026 is the alarm. Germany's 2027 procurement draft +55 percent to EUR 30bn; the EUR 100bn fund's exhaustion.

- FY2026 order intake: modal about EUR 580m; alarm H2 book-to-bill below 0.9x; invalidate FY2026 intake below FY2025's EUR 475.2m. Two consecutive intake misses with the gross margin not recovering is the sector's sign of real loss.

- FY2026 revenue: guidance upper end of EUR 460m to 500m; our modal EUR 500m; consensus EUR 505m; alarm H2 2026 revenue below EUR 285m. FY2026 EBIT: guidance EUR 53m to 58m; our modal EUR 58m; consensus EUR 59.4m; alarm below EUR 55m; invalidate below EUR 53m.
- Gross margin: our modal 22 to 23 percent for FY2026; alarm FY2026 below 22 percent; invalidate FY2027 below 20 percent for a full year.
